data.narrative:
Code Metal, a Series B-stage defense and security company, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 10 peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms. The peer set for stage-matched valuation comprises 6 same-sector, same-stage companies including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Castelion ($1.0B), Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), and Heven AeroTech ($1.0B).

Two valuation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the company's last post-money valuation of $1.2B, implying $2.4B. The Peer-Median approach benchmarks Code Metal against the 6 same-stage peers, yielding a median valuation of $1.0B (range: $300M–$3.0B). Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $850M to $2.7B, with a median of $1.7B.

The current post-money valuation of $1.25B sits near the peer median but below the stage-progression implied value, suggesting modest upside to $1.7B under a balanced scenario. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer valuations (10x spread) and the materiality of differentiation factors not captured in stage and sector filtering. Additional downside to $850M would obtain if Code Metal underperforms relative to peers; upside to $2.7B depends on trajectory acceleration versus the stage-typical 1.9x multiplier.
